panels.title: Lottery activity
panels.description: Running = a round started and has not finished yet (a proxy over a 70 minute window, which covers the typical ~50 minute length). For rare events (2 rounds in 12 hours) a timeline reads far better than a rate-based time series. Venue (PUMP/DEX) is not split out yet: lottery.start events carry no venue/pool field. We will add it when they do.

targets.expr: ((sum(count_over_time({container_name="lottery-buyer"} | json | event="lottery.start" [70m])) or vector(0)) - (sum(count_over_time({container_name="lottery-buyer"} | json | event="lottery.complete" [70m])) or vector(0)) - (sum(count_over_time({container_name="lottery-buyer"} | json | event="api.lottery_failed" [70m])) or vector(0))) > bool 0

panels.title: Token buy outcomes / min
panels.description: The fate of individual tokens inside rounds: bought, threw an exception, skipped (zero budget).

panels.title: Lotteries started (24h)
panels.description: How many rounds started over 24 hours.

panels.title: Lotteries successful (24h)
panels.description: Rounds that reached lottery.complete over 24 hours (the successful path, not to be confused with failed). Failed rounds are counted through api.lottery_failed — see Lottery success %.

panels.title: Token buys completed (24h)
panels.description: How many tokens were bought successfully (lottery.token_buy_complete) over 24 hours.

panels.title: Token buys failed (24h)
panels.description: How many tokens threw an exception in batchBuy over 24 hours.

panels.title: Tokens skipped — budget=0 (24h)
panels.description: Tokens skipped because of a zero budget after the reserves were subtracted. An informational metric, not an error.

panels.title: Lottery success %
panels.description: The share of successful rounds among FINISHED ones (complete + failed) over 24 hours. In-progress rounds are not in the denominator.

panels.title: Purchase outcomes / min
panels.description: Purchases per minute: completed vs abandoned (all causes). The main health indicator for buying.

panels.title: Slippage retry / min
panels.description: The instant retry on a slippage error: fired and failed. If slippage_retry_failed is rising, the configured slippage is too low.

panels.title: Purchases completed (24h)
panels.description: Total successful purchases over 24 hours.

panels.title: Purchases abandoned (24h)
panels.description: Total purchases that gave up (every abandoned_* cause).

panels.title: Purchase success %
panels.description: The share of completed out of completed + abandoned over 24 hours. The main health indicator for buying. Below 95% is worth digging into.

panels.title: Pending confirmed (24h)
panels.description: Transactions where PostSendError turned out to be a false alarm: the tx did go through. No money was lost.

panels.title: Venue distribution (24h)
panels.description: The share of purchases by venue: pumpfun (bonding curve), dex (Jupiter directly), fallback (pumpfun failed and it switched to dex).

panels.title: Venue purchases / min
panels.description: The rate of purchases by venue in real time. When pumpfun drops, dex rises (the fallback).

panels.title: Pumpfun completed (24h)
panels.description: Direct purchases on the pump.fun bonding curve over 24 hours.

panels.title: DEX completed (24h)
panels.description: Direct purchases through Jupiter (the token has already graduated) over 24 hours.

panels.title: Fallback pf→dex (24h)
panels.description: Purchases where pumpfun failed before sending and the system switched to Jupiter. Yellow at 3+, red at 10+.

panels.title: Fallback rate %
panels.description: The share of purchases that finished through the fallback, out of all completed. A high percentage means pumpfun fails often.

targets.expr: (sum(count_over_time({container_name="lottery-buyer"} | json | event="buy.fallback.pumpfun_to_dex" [24h])) or vector(0)) / sum(count_over_time({container_name="lottery-buyer"} | json | event="purchase.completed" [24h]))

panels.title: Retry phase activity / min
panels.description: The retry phase: how many attempts started, how many succeeded, how many failed. High attempts with low success means RPC or liquidity has degraded.

panels.title: Deferred & window expired / min
panels.description: deferred_to_retry means the purchase went into the retry buffer. window_expired means the retry window ran out and the purchase was given up. A rise in the second means the retry buffer is too short.

panels.title: Retry attempts (24h)
panels.description: Total retry attempts over 24 hours.

panels.title: Retry succeeded (24h)
panels.description: Retry attempts that saved a purchase.

panels.title: Retry success %
panels.description: The share of successful retries among FINISHED retry attempts (success + failed). In-flight attempts are not in the denominator. A low value means retries are not helping and the problem is systemic.

panels.title: Slippage retries triggered (24h)
panels.description: How many times the instant retry fired on a slippage error over 24 hours.

panels.title: Send rounds / min
panels.description: Token deliveries to recipients: successful batches, failed batches, empty rounds (nothing to send).

panels.title: Send edge cases / min
panels.description: Special cases: compute limit split (the batch was too large), carry-forward (balance=0, postponed), last-round retry success (saved in the final round).

panels.title: Sends completed (24h)
panels.description: Successful batch deliveries over 24 hours.

panels.title: Sends failed (24h)
panels.description: Failed batch deliveries over 24 hours. Any value > 0 means some recipients did not get their tokens.

panels.title: Send success %
panels.description: The share of successful batch deliveries. A critical metric: whether the tokens reach the people who backed a coin depends on it.

panels.title: Carry-forward (24h)
panels.description: A send was postponed because balance=0 (the buying is still running). Normal for early rounds; a rise towards the end of a round is a problem.

panels.title: Last-round retry ok (24h)
panels.description: A last-chance retry in the final round saved a delivery. Every value is one delivery rescued.

panels.title: Compute limit splits (24h)
panels.description: A batch exceeded the compute limit and was split into smaller parts. Up to 5 a day is normal; more means the default batch size should go up.

panels.title: Batch lifecycle / min
panels.description: batch.init (start), batch.retry_start (the retry window opening), batch.complete (finish). The gap between init and complete is the batch duration.

panels.title: API events / min
panels.description: The API layer: finished and failed /execute calls, plus internal endpoint errors.

panels.title: Batches started (24h)
panels.description: batch.init — how many batch purchases started over 24 hours (one per token per round).

panels.title: Batches completed (24h)
panels.description: batch.complete — how many batch purchases reached the finish.

panels.title: API lotteries completed (24h)
panels.description: Fire-and-forget rounds that the backend marked finished through the API.

panels.title: API errors (24h)
panels.description: api.lottery_failed + api.execute_error + api.state_read_error. Anything > 0 is a problem with the API integration.

panels.title: Info & debug logs
panels.description: Every info and debug log line from the buyer. Filter by event for a particular event type, and by lotteryId for a particular round.
